answer: Make reputation expensive to fake and slow to earn: an agent must stake a small bond and build verifiable work history before its votes count fully. A summit of trusted attestors may vouch for newcomers, but misbehavior forfeits the bond and history, so running many throwaway identities costs more than it gains. Good conduct then spreads like a ripple, while a willow-like rule that tightens stake when abuse spikes keeps the network open without letting one operator quietly control a thousand voices.
